summary: Initial discovery for Solace Medical evaluating Redwood for embedding/search and chat assistants. Main focus: quick developer onboarding (PLG), free trial credits, time-to-first-token, and security requirements (SOC2, KMS, SSO). Customer leaning toward starting with hosted API for quick eval, then pilot on Dedicated or Private pending compliance needs.
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-07-21 09:00 PT | Duration: 48m | Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Connor (Redwood SE), Dr. Elena Ruiz, Marcus Chen, Priya Nair, Aaron Lee

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone thanks for joining - I'm Maya from Redwood, appreciate you carving out time. Quick intro round?
[00:12] Dr. Elena: Hi I'm Elena, head of data at Solace Medical. We're exploring LLMs for clinical note summarization and question-answer assistants.
[00:18] Marcus: Marcus here, engineering manager, I'll own infra side.
[00:22] Priya: Priya, compliance - SOC2, HIPAA-ish questions.
[00:26] Aaron: Aaron, ML infra.
[00:29] Maya: Great - Connor and Jared are with me, Connor is our platform SE, Jared does benchmarking and SDKs. Connor, quick hello?
[00:38] Connor: Hey team. Quick note - we'll focus on low friction dev experience (time-to-first-token), and also how to scale if you move to dedicated or private.
[00:46] Marcus: Sounds good. High level we care about latency for real-time chat in clinician workflow, cost for scale, and data residency / encryption.
[00:55] Maya: Perfect, I put a short agenda in the calendar invite: 1) quickstart and free credits 2) hosted vs dedicated vs private tradeoffs 3) security checklist and next steps.

[01:10] Connor: For the PLG flow, typical steps - sign up, get free credits, follow quickstart repo, call the REST API or SDK, get first token in minutes. We provide sample apps in Python/Node; Jared will share the repo.
[01:28] Aaron: Is that the same for embeddings and chat?
[01:31] Connor: Yep. Embeddings + text gen + chat streaming are supported. The hosted API gives fastest time to first token. For embeddings you can use the same key and endpoints.

[01:45] Marcus: Roughly what's the expected latency for hosted? Our median target is sub-300ms for single-turn chat under 512 tokens.
[01:53] Connor: Typical medians for our curated open models on hosted are 120-250ms at 512 tokens depending on model. If you want lower latency we can route to Dedicated pools or smaller models. Note that tokenization and network also add variability.
[02:10] Dr. Elena: What about cost per embedding - ballpark?
[02:14] Maya: We have usage tiers - for the PLG trial you'll get credits. Post-trial pricing depends on model family and quantization. For embeddings it's lower rate than generation. I'll send current pricing sheet - but for a quick sense, our open model embeddings are typically a fraction of big closed models.

[02:35] Priya: On security: do you support SSO, RBAC, KMS? We need audit logs and separation for PHI.
[02:41] Connor: Yes. Hosted supports SSO (SAML/Okta), RBAC for teams, audit logs and optional bring-your-own-key (BYOK) through KMS. For PHI we usually recommend Dedicated or Private so data doesn't touch multi-tenant cache policies.
[02:59] Priya: So hosted might not satisfy HIPAA?
[03:04] Maya: Hosted can be acceptable if you use VPC egress controls and BYOK, but many healthcare customers start hosted for proof-of-concept and then move to Dedicated or Private for production with strict PHI requirements. We'll share a healthcare compliance note.

[03:25] Marcus: Can we get a trial account to test end-to-end? We want to run embedding similarity and a small chat UI integration.
[03:31] Maya: Yes - we'll provision trial with free credits. Connor will set up a sandbox org and invite Aaron and Marcus.
[03:38] Connor: I'll do that after the call. I'll also add a sample notebook for embeddings + an express/Flask sample that does streaming.

[03:50] Dr. Elena: On time-to-first-token, how fast? If a dev signs up now, can they actually be calling the API within an hour?
[03:58] Jared: Usually yes - sign up, verify email, grab API key, run quickstart sample. For many teams it's minutes. If you need SSO onboarding, that adds time.
[04:09] Aaron: Any SDK differences for Python vs Node?
[04:12] Connor: APIs are consistent. The SDKs wrap streaming and retries. We'll share SDK snippets. Some transcriptions show product names wrong e.g. 'Red Wood Dedicated' occasionally in docs.

[04:26] Marcus: For the pilot, we want a performance benchmark: throughput across 100 concurrent chat sessions. Can Redwood Dedicated handle this?
[04:35] Connor: Yes, Dedicated is designed for predictable throughput. You can reserve GPU pools and set autoscaling/burst policies. For 100 concurrent websockets we typically recommend pooling across multiple GPUs and tuning batch size. Jared can prepare a benchmark script to mimic your traffic.

[04:52] Dr. Elena: About caching - is there prefix caching or KV cache? We want to avoid re-embedding repeated phrases.
[04:59] Connor: We support KV cache for generation and prefix caching strategies. For embeddings you can cache vectors in your store and avoid re-requests. Redwood also has an Optimize toolkit that suggests batching and caching configs.

[05:15] Priya: Audit logs and retention - can we export logs to our SIEM?
[05:20] Connor: Yes, audit logs can be exported to S3 or a customer SIEM via connectors. Retention policies configurable on Dedicated/Private. Hosted has default retention but we can customize with an enterprise add-on.

[05:34] Maya: Quick question - what success criteria are you using for the pilot? Latency, cost per 1000 requests, and accuracy?
[05:42] Dr. Elena: Yes those three. We'll measure F1/ROUGE for summarization, token latency, and cost per 1k tokens. Also stakeholder signoff from compliance.

[05:54] Marcus: Timeline: we'd like a week to do integration and then two weeks of benchmarking. Goal to decide in 6 weeks.
[06:02] Maya: Sounds aligned with a PLG-first approach - start hosted trial, run benchmarks, then discuss Dedicated/Private for prod.

[06:12] Connor: A few tradeoffs to call out: hosted = fastest onboarding, lower operational overhead; dedicated = predictable latency/cost and isolation; private = full control for regulated data but longer setup time. Also model variants: quantized models reduce cost but may impact output quality.

[06:35] Aaron: Do you support bringing our own models? We have a fine-tuned model on Mistral architecture.
[06:41] Jared: We can run customer models in Private deployments and in some Dedicated setups. For hosted, we curate models but can host private model artifacts in Dedicated. We'll need to discuss licensing and compatibility.

[06:57] Priya: Any SOC2/HIPAA references you can send?
[07:01] Maya: Yes - prioritized. I'll attach SOC2 report, HIPAA note, and our security whitepaper.

[07:08] Marcus: API keys - rotateable? Can we do short-lived keys for service accounts?
[07:13] Connor: Keys are rotateable; we also support short-lived tokens via our control plane and SSO integrations.

[07:20] Dr. Elena: For embeddings similarity, recommended dimensionality and batching?
[07:25] Jared: Typical is 1024-1536 dims depending on model. Batch embeddings to 128-256 vectors per request to be cost efficient. We'll include suggested configs in the quickstart.

[07:40] Marcus: If we hit a performance regression after model upgrade, do you support rollbacks?
[07:44] Connor: Yes - the Console has rollouts and automatic fallback policies. You can canary new model versions and rollback if metrics degrade.

[07:55] Aaron: Any gotchas for streaming over WebSockets?
[07:58] Connor: Manage connection lifecycles and backpressure; we have client libraries that implement streaming with retries. We can share sample code.

[08:07] Priya: Data residency - can we pin region to eu-west-1?
[08:11] Maya: Yes, you can pin to regions. For PHI we often recommend Dedicated or Private in the target region. Hosted has region controls for account provisioning as well.

[08:25] Marcus: Let's talk concrete next steps - Aaron and Marcus will run the quickstart this week, Priya will review the security docs, Elena will define the eval prompts.
[08:34] Maya: We'll provision trial, send guide and notebook, and schedule a SE-led benchmarking session next Wednesday.

[08:42] Connor: I'll also drop a sample benchmark script and a link to the quickstart repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/quickstart and our deck: https://redwood.ai/decks/plg-quickstart.pdf.

[08:58] Dr. Elena: One more question - if we escalate to Dedicated, what's lead time?
[09:02] Jared: Dedicated typically 2-4 weeks depending on capacity and config. Private/on-prem longer (4-8+ weeks).

[09:12] Marcus: Ok makes sense.

[09:15] Maya: Recap of next steps: Maya to send pricing + docs; Connor to set up trial; Jared to prepare benchmark script; Priya to send compliance questions. We'll reconvene after the initial trial.

[09:30] Dr. Elena: Thanks everyone - excited to try it out.

[09:33] Maya: Thanks all, we'll follow up with links and invites.

[09:36] (call ends)

Notes on transcript: occasional mis-transcriptions: 'Redwood Dedicated' was sometimes rendered as 'Red Wood Dedicated', 'KV cache' occasionally 'K V cache'. Natural speech, interruptions and clarifying questions present. References shared: quickstart repo, PLG deck, benchmark spreadsheet (link shared during follow-up).
